answer:
Use **`FunctionAgent`**, the prebuilt agent in LlamaIndex's workflow-based agent API. Import it from `llama_index.core.agent.workflow`: "from llama_index.core.agent.workflow import FunctionAgent" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]

You pass it an LLM and a list of tools: "agent = FunctionAgent(" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]. The example in that file passes a plain Python function, `multiply`, as a tool, with the docstring describing what it does: "Useful for multiplying two numbers." [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]

Tools can be more than plain functions. The agent is "given a set of tools, which can be anything from arbitrary functions up to full LlamaIndex query engines" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/understanding/agent/index.md].

If you need custom control flow beyond a prebuilt agent, the docs point to building your own agentic workflows with LlamaIndex Workflows [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/understanding/agent/index.md]. The excerpts don't say more about that option, so I don't know its details from them.
